paper_title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models Non-linearity, Sparsity, and   Attention-Sink-Free
caption: Distribution of gating scores under different constraints for SDPA output gating variants.

model_annotations.Bulgarian:
The provided figure illustrates the distribution of gating scores across layers for different statistical measures (mean, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum) of an output gating mechanism in a large language model. The horizontal axis represents the layer index, ranging from 0 to 22, with integer labels at each whole number. The vertical axis represents the gate value, scaled linearly from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks and labels at intervals of 0.2. Four distinct lines represent the statistical measures: the mean is shown as a blue dashed line with circular markers; the standard deviation is an orange dotted line with circular markers; the minimum is a green dashed line with triangular markers; and the maximum is a red solid line with circular markers.

The mean (blue dashed line) begins near 0.05 at layer 0, rises to approximately 0.3 at layer 5, continues to increase to a peak near 0.45 at layer 15, then declines to about 0.25 by layer 22. The standard deviation (orange dotted line) starts near 0.05, remains relatively low and stable around 0.1 until layer 10, then gradually increases to approximately 0.2 by layer 22. The minimum (green dashed line) stays very close to 0.0 throughout the entire range, with minor fluctuations, dipping slightly below 0.0 at some points, but remaining consistently near zero. The maximum (red solid line) begins at approximately 0.55 at layer 0, drops sharply to around 0.2 at layer 3, then rises to a peak near 0.95 at layer 15, remains relatively stable around 0.90–0.95 from layer 15 to layer 20, and slightly decreases to about 0.90 by layer 22.
model_annotations.Chinese: This line chart, titled "atten_output_gate_head_share gate values," displays the distribution of gating scores for different statistical constraints—mean, standard deviation (std), minimum (min), and maximum (max)—across layers in a model, as referenced in the paper "Gated Attention for Large Language Models Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free." The y-axis, labeled "gate value," ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 in a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The x-axis, labeled "layer," spans from 0 to 20, also on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The chart includes four lines: the mean is represented by a blue dashed line with circular markers; the standard deviation is shown as an orange dotted line with circular markers; the minimum is depicted as a green dashed line with triangular markers; and the maximum is shown as a solid red line with circular markers. The mean line starts near 0.05, rises to a peak of approximately 0.45 at layer 15, and then declines to about 0.2 at layer 20. The standard deviation line remains relatively flat, hovering between 0.05 and 0.2, with a slight upward trend. The minimum line stays very low, fluctuating between 0.0 and 0.05, with a slight increase around layer 15. The maximum line begins at approximately 0.55, dips to a low of about 0.2 at layer 5, then rises sharply to a peak of 1.0 at layer 15, and subsequently fluctuates between 0.9 and 1.0 for the remainder of the layers.
model_annotations.German: The line chart displays the distribution of gating scores for different variants of output gating in SDPA, plotted against the layer index. The x-axis represents the layer, ranging from 0 to 22, with tick marks at regular intervals of approximately 5 units, and is labeled “layer”. The y-axis represents the gate value, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at regular intervals of 0.2, and is labeled “gate value”. Four lines are shown: the mean (blue dashed line) starts at approximately 0.05, rises to a peak of about 0.48 at layer 16, and ends near 0.25 at layer 22; the standard deviation (orange dotted line) begins near 0.05, fluctuates slightly, and ends near 0.18; the minimum (green dashed line) remains near 0.0 throughout, with minor fluctuations; and the maximum (red solid line) starts at approximately 0.55, drops to a minimum of about 0.20 at layer 7, rises to a peak of 1.0 at layer 15, and ends near 0.95 at layer 22.
